newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Oil shares rise in dull Nigerian trading.
newsitem.headline: Oil shares rise in dull Nigerian trading.

text.p: Oil shares rose in dull trade on Monday at the Nigerian stock market, traders said.
The all-share index closed hardly changed at 6654.49 from 6654.50 on Friday as key stocks continued to slide.
"For sometime, the market has been down despite the fall in interest rate," one trader said. "If there were no oil sector, the market would have been silent."
Cadbury was still undr pressure, ending 10 kobo down at 25.70 naira while conglomerate Lever Brothers fell five kobo to 25.15 naira.
Union Bank, one of the country's big three, also fell by 30 kobo to 6.70 naira. Guinness went 10 kobo lower to 6.60 naira.
Oil shares, the toast of the Nigerian market, remained active although investors showed equally healthy interest in Nigerian Breweries and Benue Cement.
Benue Cement finished 36 kobo up to close at 7.66 naira while the brewing giant chalked 35 kobo to 11.55 naira.
Top oil gainer was Unipetrol, up 21 kobo at 47.51 naira, followed by Total with a 20 kobo gain to 50.70 naira.
Food stocks Nestle and Union Dicon Salt each rose 10 kobo to 40.20 naira and 39.50 naira, respectively while construction firm Cappa and D'Alberto added 13 kobo to 5.83 naira.
